Definition: from G4862 and G1210; to bind with, i.e. (passively) be a fellow-prisoner (figuratively):--be bound with.
BiblicalUsage: The writer of Hebrews says to remember those in bonds as bound with them, and those who suffer adversity, as being yourselves also in the body. To be bound with prisoners is to count their chains as your own, because the same body that holds you holds them.
TheologicalSignificance: What grips me is that remembering prisoners as if bound with them is the heart of Christian love, and I hold that I am my brother's keeper when he is in chains.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
